name: Angelite
spiritual: Said to link to angelic guides
physical: Traditionally associated with relaxation and restful sleep
Kept nearby for comfort during stressful times
Linked by crystal healers to easy, relaxed breathing
summary: Angelite is the soft sky-blue anhydrite from Peru, a gentle stone linked to peaceful sleep, compassionate speech and a sense of angelic presence.
intro: Angelite is a dusty, sky-blue stone that looks as if a bit of cloud was pressed into a pebble. It is the trade name for blue anhydrite, found mainly in Peru, and tumbled pieces often show white mottling, soft streaks and a slightly powdery shine. The color is sometimes faint, almost lavender-grey, and in the best pieces it is a calm, steady blue. It is soft and a bit fragile, so it is cut into palm stones, spheres, hearts and cabochons rather than hard-wearing jewelry. It is a staple of angel-themed collections and a beloved bedside stone.
history: Anhydrite was named in 1804 for its lack of water, but blue Peruvian anhydrite was not marketed as angelite until the 1980s, when a Peruvian deposit found in 1987 was introduced to the crystal trade. The new name reflected its heavenly color and the associations practitioners had with it. The stone is a recent addition to the crystal repertoire, with no ancient folk tradition. Many early specimens were sold under the label celestite or blue anhydrite until the name angelite became standard.
meaning: Angelite is called the stone of the angels in crystal circles. People use it to feel a sense of calm protection, to say the things that are hard to say and to sleep more peacefully. It is linked to the throat, third eye and crown, and is said to encourage compassion in conversations as well as gentle self-forgiveness. Practitioners place it near the bed to encourage peaceful dreams, or in prayer spaces to feel less alone. Emotionally it is described as lowering the volume on anxious thoughts. Traditionally it is also tied to relaxed breathing and a restful body. It is not a flashy stone, but a quietly comforting one, often favored by people who want softness.
howToUse: Hold angelite in your hand while you set an intention before sleep, then place it on the nightstand. Keep a palm stone nearby during conversations where you want to stay kind but honest. Rest it on the throat or third eye for a short meditation. Add it to a grid with selenite and clear quartz for calm. Angelite also makes a lovely gift for someone who is grieving or anxious, as a small reminder of softness.
care: Angelite is soft and sensitive to water and humidity, so keep it dry and wipe with a soft cloth. Avoid long sun exposure, which can fade the blue. Cleanse by sound, breath, smoke or moonlight, and avoid salt, which can damage the surface. Store in a pouch away from harder stones. Never put it in the shower or wear it in water.
identify: Genuine angelite is a soft, hazy, pale blue with a waxy look, often slightly mottled with white. It is easily confused with blue calcite, celestite, blue lace agate and dyed howlite. Dyed howlite is chalky with dark veins, and calcite fizzes in vinegar. Real angelite is heavier than it looks and scratches with a copper coin. Some pieces are stabilized to prevent crumbling, which is a common practice.

faq.a: In crystal tradition angelite is used for peaceful sleep, calm communication and a feeling of angelic presence. People keep it by the bed, on prayer altars or in a pocket when they need softness.

faq.q: Is angelite the same as celestite?
faq.a: No. Angelite is blue anhydrite, a calcium sulfate, while celestite is strontium sulfate. They look similar, but celestite is usually more crystalline and angelite is more hazy and massive.
It is best kept dry. Angelite is soft and reacts slowly with water, so soaking can weaken it. Wipe it with a soft dry cloth and cleanse with moonlight, sound or breath.
